q-12983.problem: The equation $4{z}^{2}+4z=12$ can be written in the form $(z+p)^{2}=q.$ Find $p+q,$ and solve the equation.
q-12983.worked_solution:
First, we move the constant term to the right-hand side, divide it by the coefficient of the quadratic term, and complete the square on the left-hand side.

$$
\begin{aligned}4{z}^{2}+4z & =12 \\ 4({z}^{2}+z) & =12 \\ {z}^{2}+z & =3 \\ {z}^{2}+2\cdot \frac{1}{2}\cdot z & =3 \\ {z}^{2}+2\cdot (\frac{1}{2})\cdot z+{(\frac{1}{2})}^{2}-{(\frac{1}{2})}^{2} & =3 \\ {(z+\frac{1}{2})}^{2}-{(\frac{1}{2})}^{2} & =3\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we isolate the perfect square:

$$
\begin{aligned}{(z+\frac{1}{2})}^{2}-{(\frac{1}{2})}^{2} & =3 \\ {(z+\frac{1}{2})}^{2}-\frac{1}{4} & =\frac{12}{4} \\ {(z+\frac{1}{2})}^{2} & =\frac{13}{4}\end{aligned}
$$

So, $p=\frac{1}{2},q=\frac{13}{4},$ and $p+q=\frac{15}{4}.$ 

Next, we solve the equation using the square-root method:

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt{{(z+\frac{1}{2})}^{2}} & =\sqrt{\frac{13}{4}} \\ |z+\frac{1}{2}| & =\frac{\sqrt{13}}{2} \\ z+\frac{1}{2} & =\pm \frac{\sqrt{13}}{2} \\ z & =-\frac{1}{2}\pm \frac{\sqrt{13}}{2} \\ z & =\frac{-1\pm \sqrt{13}}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

q-60361.problem: The equation $4{x}^{2}-6x-3=0$ can be written in the form $4(x+p)^{2}=q.$ Find $p,$ and solve the equation.
q-60361.worked_solution:
First, we move the constant term to the right-hand side, factor the coefficient of the quadratic term, and complete the square on the left-hand side.

$$
\begin{aligned}4{x}^{2}-6x-3 & =0 \\ 4{x}^{2}-6x & =3 \\ 4[{x}^{2}-\frac{3}{2}x] & =3 \\ 4[{x}^{2}-2\cdot \frac{3}{4}x+{(\frac{3}{4})}^{2}-{(\frac{3}{4})}^{2}] & =3 \\ 4[{(x-\frac{3}{4})}^{2}-\frac{9}{16}] & =3\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we expand the brackets, and write the equation in the required form:

$$
\begin{aligned}4{(x-\frac{3}{4})}^{2}-4\cdot \frac{9}{16} & =3 \\ 4{(x-\frac{3}{4})}^{2}-\frac{9}{4} & =3 \\ 4{(x-\frac{3}{4})}^{2} & =3+\frac{9}{4} \\ 4{(x-\frac{3}{4})}^{2} & =\frac{21}{4}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $p=-\frac{3}{4}.$ We now solve the equation using the square root method:

$$
\begin{aligned}4{(x-\frac{3}{4})}^{2} & =\frac{21}{4} \\ {(x-\frac{3}{4})}^{2} & =\frac{21}{16} \\ \sqrt{{(x-\frac{3}{4})}^{2}} & =\sqrt{\frac{21}{16}} \\ |x-\frac{3}{4}| & =\sqrt{\frac{21}{16}} \\ x-\frac{3}{4} & =\pm \sqrt{\frac{21}{16}} \\ x-\frac{3}{4} & =\pm \frac{\sqrt{21}}{4} \\ x & =\frac{3}{4}\pm \frac{\sqrt{21}}{4} \\ x & =\frac{3\pm \sqrt{21}}{4}\end{aligned}
$$

The equation 4x2−6x−3=0 can be written in the form 4(x+p)2=q. Find p, and solve the equation.

a
p=−34,x=3±214
b
p=34,x=3±214
c
p=−34,x=6±214
d
p=214,x=6±214
e
p=−214,x=3±214
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, we move the constant term to the right-hand side, factor the coefficient of the quadratic term, and complete the square on the left-hand side.

4x2−6x−3=04x2−6x=34[x2−32x]=34[x2−2⋅34x+(34)2−(34)2]=34[(x−34)2−916]=3

Next, we expand the brackets, and write the equation in the required form:

4(x−34)2−4⋅916=34(x−34)2−94=34(x−34)2=3+944(x−34)2=214

Therefore, p=−34. We now solve the equation using the square root method:

4(x−34)2=214(x−34)2=2116(x−34)2=2116|x−34|=2116x−34=±2116x−34=±214x=34±214x=3±214

q-86414.problem: The equation $-3{x}^{2}+36x-94=0$ can be written in the form $3(x+p)^{2}=q.$ Find $q-p.$
q-86414.worked_solution:
First, we multiply the equation by $-1$:

$$
\begin{aligned}(-1)\cdot (-3{x}^{2}+36x-94) & =(-1)\cdot 0 \\ 3{x}^{2}-36x+94 & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we move the constant term to the right-hand side, factor the coefficient of the quadratic term, and complete the square on the left-hand side.

$$
\begin{aligned}3{x}^{2}-36x+94 & =0 \\ 3{x}^{2}-36x & =-94 \\ 3[{x}^{2}-12x] & =-94 \\ 3[{x}^{2}-2\cdot 6x+{6}^{2}-{6}^{2}] & =-94 \\ 3[{(x-6)}^{2}-36] & =-94\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we isolate the perfect square:

$$
\begin{aligned}3{(x-6)}^{2}-3\cdot 36 & =-94 \\ 3{(x-6)}^{2}-108 & =-94 \\ 3{(x-6)}^{2} & =-94+108 \\ 3{(x-6)}^{2} & =14\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $p=-6$, $q=14.$ Finally,

$$
q-p=14-(-6)=14+6=20.
$$

q-112589.problem: The equation $6{z}^{2}+10z-1=0$ can be written in the form $6(z+p)^{2}=q.$ Find $p+q.$
q-112589.worked_solution:
First, we move the constant term to the right-hand side, factor the coefficient of the quadratic term, and complete the square on the left-hand side.

$$
\begin{aligned}6{z}^{2}+10z-1 & =0 \\ 6{z}^{2}+10z & =1 \\ 6({z}^{2}+\frac{5}{3}z) & =1 \\ 6[{z}^{2}+2\cdot \frac{5}{6}\cdot z+{(\frac{5}{6})}^{2}-{(\frac{5}{6})}^{2}] & =1 \\ 6[{(z+\frac{5}{6})}^{2}-{(\frac{5}{6})}^{2}] & =1 \\ 6[{(z+\frac{5}{6})}^{2}-\frac{25}{36}] & =1\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we expand the brackets, and write the equation in the required form:

$$
\begin{aligned}6{(z+\frac{5}{6})}^{2}-6\cdot \frac{25}{36} & =1 \\ 6{(z+\frac{5}{6})}^{2}-\frac{25}{6} & =1 \\ 6{(z+\frac{5}{6})}^{2} & =\frac{31}{6}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $p=\frac{5}{6}$ and $q=\frac{31}{6}.$ Finally,

$$
p+q=\frac{5}{6}+\frac{31}{6}=\frac{36}{6}=6.
$$

q-112614.problem: The equation $-2{x}^{2}-16x-23=0$ can be written in the form $2(x+p)^{2}=q.$ Find $q,$ and solve the equation.
q-112614.worked_solution:
First, we multiply the equation by $-1:$

$$
\begin{aligned}(-1)\cdot (-2{x}^{2}-16x-23) & =(-1)\cdot 0 \\ 2{x}^{2}+16x+23 & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Now we move the constant term to the right-hand side, factor the coefficient of the quadratic term, and complete the square on the left-hand side.

$$
\begin{aligned}2{x}^{2}+16x+23 & =0 \\ 2{x}^{2}+16x & =-23 \\ 2({x}^{2}+8x) & =-23 \\ 2[{x}^{2}+2\cdot 4\cdot x+{4}^{2}-{4}^{2}] & =-23 \\ 2[{(x+4)}^{2}-16] & =-23\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we expand the brackets, and write the equation in the required form:

$$
\begin{aligned}2{(x+4)}^{2}-2\cdot 16 & =-23 \\ 2{(x+4)}^{2}-32 & =-23 \\ 2{(x+4)}^{2} & =-23+32 \\ 2{(x+4)}^{2} & =9\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $q=9.$ We now solve the equation using the square root method:

$$
\begin{aligned}2{(x+4)}^{2} & =9 \\ {(x+4)}^{2} & =\frac{9}{2} \\ \sqrt{{(x+4)}^{2}} & =\sqrt{\frac{9}{2}} \\ |x+4| & =\frac{3}{\sqrt{2}} \\ x+4 & =\pm \frac{3\sqrt{2}}{2} \\ x & =-4\pm \frac{3\sqrt{2}}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

The equation −2x2−16x−23=0 can be written in the form 2(x+p)2=q. Find q, and solve the equation.

a
q=4,x=−1±322
b
q=4,x=−1±22
c
q=9,x=−4±322
d
q=9,x=−2±324
e
q=9,x=−6±322
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, we multiply the equation by −1:

(−1)⋅(−2x2−16x−23)=(−1)⋅02x2+16x+23=0

Now we move the constant term to the right-hand side, factor the coefficient of the quadratic term, and complete the square on the left-hand side.

2x2+16x+23=02x2+16x=−232(x2+8x)=−232[x2+2⋅4⋅x+42−42]=−232[(x+4)2−16]=−23

Next, we expand the brackets, and write the equation in the required form:

2(x+4)2−2⋅16=−232(x+4)2−32=−232(x+4)2=−23+322(x+4)2=9

Therefore, q=9. We now solve the equation using the square root method:

2(x+4)2=9(x+4)2=92(x+4)2=92|x+4|=32x+4=±322x=−4±322
